title: Equivalent Pseudo-angular Momentum Governs Selective Magnon-Phonon Hybridization
authors: Hong Sun, Hao Chen, Lifa Zhang
abstract: Magnon-phonon hybridization provides a powerful route to couple spin and lattice excitations, yet the symmetry principle governing mode selectivity remains unclear. Here, we show that crystalline pseudoangular momentum provides a general criterion for selective magnon-phonon hybridization in noncollinear multisublattice magnetic systems. The rotation eigenvalue associated with pseudoangular momentum encodes polarization transformations, sublattice permutations, and Bloch phases, requiring magnetoelastic coupling between modes belonging to the same rotation sector. We illustrate this principle in a stacked kagome model with noncollinear spin order. An out-of-plane magnetic field tunes one magnon sector into resonance with a degenerate phonon doublet, yet only the pseudoangular-momentum-matched phonon develops a pronounced avoided crossing while the other remains nearly unmixed. Field reversal switches the selected rotation sector and reverses the rotational polarization of the hybridized phonon component without changing the hybrid-mode energies. Our results reveal pseudoangular-momentum matching as a general framework for understanding and controlling mode-selective spin-lattice hybridization.
summary: This work introduces crystalline pseudoangular momentum as a fundamental symmetry rule governing how magnons and phonons interact in complex magnetic materials. By applying this rule to a stacked kagome model, the authors show that hybridization is not just determined by energy resonance, but by the matching of these pseudoangular momenta. This provides a general framework for controlling spin-lattice coupling in noncollinear magnets.
main_problem: The paper addresses the unclear symmetry principle governing selective magnon-phonon hybridization in complex, noncollinear magnetic systems.
main_result: Crystalline pseudoangular momentum provides a general symmetry criterion dictating that only magnon-phonon pairs matching this momentum can hybridize strongly, allowing for symmetry-controlled mode selectivity.
method: The analysis involves deriving the magnetoelastic coupling Hamiltonian based on crystal symmetry ($C_n$) and solving the resulting bosonic generalized eigenvalue problem.
model_or_system: The study uses a stacked kagome lattice model exhibiting noncollinear $120^\circ$ spin order, coupling magnetic excitations (magnons) to lattice vibrations (phonons).
key_observables: Avoided crossing in the excitation spectrum, basis-independent coupling strengths ($s_1, s_2$), and the rotational polarization of the hybridized phonon component.
important_parameters: Out-of-plane magnetic field strength ($h_z$), which tunes the system into resonance and breaks symmetry.
main_assumptions: The magnetoelastic interaction is assumed to preserve the underlying crystalline rotational symmetry ($C_n$).
figures_summary:
Figures illustrate the model geometry, the uncoupled and coupled spectra, and show how the coupling strength imbalance ($s_1 
eq s_2$) emerges when a magnetic field is applied, confirming selective hybridization.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the general symmetry constraint using pseudoangular momentum, then models the coupling via a bond-length dependent DM interaction, and finally demonstrates field-induced selectivity by analyzing the resulting spectral changes and mode decompositions.
why_interesting: The concept of pseudoangular momentum as a symmetry filter for coupling mechanisms is a powerful, generalizable tool for understanding mode selectivity in coupled quantum systems, analogous to selection rules in spectroscopy.
